scope: Approximate LIGHT/MEDIUM/RICH tendency of the exact neat INCI at equal modest leave-on dose on hair. It is not skin absorption, a benefit claim, or a formulation prediction.
method: A value is an explicitly provisional hair-relevant engineering estimate from material flow/film behavior unless evidence_basis says otherwise. Skin sensory and blend, rinse-out, or pre-wash claims are retained only as non-decisive context.
access_limits: No located source supplied a controlled, cross-oil neat leave-on human-hair heaviness/volume panel for this 16-oil set. Supplier language is grade-bound; primary hair papers below measure damage, penetration, adhesion, or film, not perceived weight.

foundational_hair_engineering_source.verified_observation: The hair-formulation review connects viscosity to spreading and perceived heaviness, and says surface coverage/spreading determine hair lubrication. It gives approximate viscosities: jojoba 40 cps; argan, almond and avocado 60-70 cps; castor about 760 cps; coconut melting point 24 C.
foundational_hair_engineering_source.limit: Technical formulation reasoning, not a controlled comparative human-hair weight or volume study.

entries.reason: Liquid wax that remains fluid; 40-cps technical reference supports light at modest dose, not a transfer from its low-greasy skin claim.
entries.verified_observation: Technical hair-formulation review reports jojoba about 40 cps and identifies it as liquid wax. No source measures hair weight.
entries.non_decisive: Folklore scalp/hair use does not rank neat leave-on weight.

entries.reason: Lower viscosity than the tested macadamia comparator supports a lower film-burden estimate at equal dose; hair feel was not tested.
entries.verified_observation: The 2024 body-oil study reports tested grapeseed below tested macadamia in viscosity at 22 C.
entries.non_decisive: Both sources are body/skin evidence, not hair volume or coating evidence.

entries.reason: Exact C8/C10 triglyceride grade is described for hair care as lightweight and low viscosity; that supports light at modest leave-on dose, with medium plausible for a nonvolatile oil.
entries.verified_observation: Inolex lists exact INCI, hair care application, and low viscosity/lightweight language; IOI lists C8/C10 grades at about 28/30 mPa s at 20 C.
entries.non_decisive: Supplier guidance is grade-bound and does not disclose a comparative neat-hair panel.

entries.reason: The technical hair-formulation reference puts almond among the easy-spreading 60-70-cps oils; no hair-weight study makes medium a credible alternative.
entries.verified_observation: The 2023 hair formulation review gives almond 60-70 cps; a 2024 body-oil study places its almond sample below macadamia in viscosity.
entries.non_decisive: The body-oil study is skin, not hair.

entries.reason: An exact-material SDS reports about 60 mPa s, near the 60-70-cps easy-spreading almond/argan reference range; light is a physical-film estimate, not a skin descriptor.
entries.verified_observation: The exact apricot-kernel SDS reports dynamic viscosity about 60 mPa s; the technical hair review calls the 60-70-cps almond/argan group easy-spreading/lightweight.
entries.non_decisive: No source tests perceived weight or volume on neat apricot oil; viscosity has unspecified measurement conditions in the SDS.

entries.reason: A comparative raw-oil data table reports safflower at 55 mPa s at room temperature, below macadamia's 73 in the same table; light is a relative surface-flow estimate.
entries.verified_observation: The patent's room-temperature raw-oil table reports safflower 55 mPa s and macadamia nut oil 73 mPa s.
entries.non_decisive: This is food/emulsion research rather than hair sensory; plain INCI does not resolve high-oleic versus high-linoleic grade.

entries.reason: Very high specified dynamic viscosity makes the largest surface-film/volume-loss tendency in this subset a responsible engineering estimate at equal dose.
entries.verified_observation: Sigma's refined castor specification reports 950-1100 mPa s; the 2024 body-oil paper reports a conflicting much lower value.
entries.non_decisive: Neither source measures hair heaviness; the viscosity conflict limits confidence and dilution can move the outcome.

entries.reason: Whole coconut's 24-C melting point plus documented hair surface-film/adhesion behavior supports a richer leave-on tendency; penetration does not prove heaviness.
entries.verified_observation: Technical review gives a 24-C melting point; hair studies report time/heat-dependent capillary adhesion and surface-film changes, and protein-loss outcomes in pre/post-wash treatment.
entries.non_decisive: Those experiments do not report perceived weight or volume; their pre-wash/grooming protocol cannot decide neat leave-on feel.

entries.reason: No affirmative material differentiator from almond was found: both are placed in the 60-70-cps easy-spreading range. Align argan with almond as light.
entries.verified_observation: Technical hair-formulation review lists argan and almond among 60-70-cps easy-spreading oils; systematic review finds no significant clinical hair-quality evidence.
entries.non_decisive: Neither source supplies a neat leave-on hair-weight comparison; common serum blends are out of scope.

entries.reason: Exact refined/virgin SDSs report roughly 70 to 90 mPa s, placing olive above the light 55-60-mPa-s comparator oils but far below castor; medium is the bounded material estimate.
entries.verified_observation: Refined olive SDS reports about 70 mPa s; extra-virgin SDS reports 80-90 mPa s at 20 C.
entries.non_decisive: The hair-fibre adhesion/penetration paper is excluded from class choice because it has no perceived-weight endpoint; olive grades vary.

entries.reason: The technical 60-70-cps range and grade spread support a middle estimate; rich remains nearest for a more residual grade or higher dose.
entries.verified_observation: Technical hair-formulation review lists avocado among 60-70-cps oils; supplier comparative material distinguishes crude avocado as greasier and refined as intermediate.
entries.non_decisive: Supplier comparison is skin only and INCI does not disclose grade.

entries.reason: Retain user-approved light/low. Supplier describes ordinary and high-oleic rows as fairly light, but this remains an uncalibrated material estimate rather than a hair outcome.
entries.verified_observation: Heess calls both sunflower rows fairly light; hair papers find no protein-loss reduction and report film/adhesion mechanics.
entries.non_decisive: Protein-loss, penetration, and pre/post-wash data do not rank leave-on heaviness; plain INCI does not specify oleic grade.

entries.reason: A room-temperature raw-oil table reports macadamia nut oil at 73 mPa s versus safflower at 55; medium is a relative flow estimate, not a default for absent hair evidence.
entries.verified_observation: The patent's raw-oil table reports macadamia nut oil 73 mPa s at room temperature.
entries.non_decisive: The table does not provide an INCI/species or hair sensory protocol, so it supports only low-confidence material comparison.

entries.reason: A primary physicochemical study reports 20-50 cP at 25 C across extracted hemp-heart-oil samples, below the cited 55-75-cP common vegetable-oil band; light is a low-confidence relative film-flow estimate.
entries.verified_observation: The hemp-heart-oil study reports Newtonian samples at 20-50 cP at 25 C, with extraction-dependent variation. The technical hair review connects lower viscosity/spreading to lighter feel.
entries.non_decisive: This is extracted hemp-heart oil rather than a cosmetic-grade leave-on panel; seed oil must not be conflated with Cannabis extracts or cannabinoids.

entries.reason: Retain user-approved medium/low. Available supplier sensory evidence conflicts from quick-matte refined skin feel to slightly-rich/rich material guidance, so the assigned value is an explicitly uncalibrated provisional choice, not hair proof.
entries.verified_observation: Kupanda describes refined marula as quick/matte on skin; O&3 describes material profiles from slightly rich to rich and lists hair applications.
entries.non_decisive: Neither source measures neat leave-on hair weight; hair-use listing and skin uptake cannot decide it.

entries.reason: An exact 100% refined baobab raw-material specification gives 25-40 cps, below the 60-70-cps almond/argan reference range; light is a modest-dose surface-flow estimate.
entries.verified_observation: Kupanda's Moyo refined 100% Adansonia Digitata Seed Oil specification reports 25-40 cps at 20 C; the technical hair review links viscosity/spreading to weight feel.
entries.non_decisive: No source measures neat leave-on hair weight; crude materials and test conditions can differ from this refined grade.
